ai_show_review.summary: Explosive Holy Trinity sequence amid muddy Fillmore East tape
ai_show_review.blurb: Features the iconic Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven run with Jerry's incendiary lead work. Sound quality is fair and often muddy, limiting listenability despite high energy throughout the set.
ai_show_review.review: The early‑night show at the Fillmore East on September 26, 1969 captures a moment of raw intensity that would become legendary in Dead lore. The band launches straight into a blistering Dark Star that segues seamlessly into Saint Stephen and then into The Eleven – what fans now call the Holy Trinity – with Jerry Garcia delivering lightning‑fast, explosive guitar lines that drive the improvisation forward. While the performance is undeniably electric, both available audience recordings suffer from fair‑to‑poor fidelity; the Hanno tape is especially muddy with limited instrument separation, and the Cotsman source shows duplication artifacts on King Bee and a glitch during Death Don't Have No Mercy. For completists willing to brave the sonic roughness, this show offers a rare glimpse of the Dead’s early exploratory spirit at one of rock’s most iconic venues.

best_recording.reason: Contains the standout Holy Trinity (Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven) despite sub‑par audio, making it the most musically significant source.
